newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB to probe temporary use of U.S. ports - Goodale.
newsitem.headline: CWB to probe temporary use of U.S. ports - Goodale.

text.p: Canadian Wheat Board will probe the possibility of temporarily using U.S. Pacific ports to ship wheat, Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said.

"The Wheat Board will investigate the utility of American transportation facilities where it will use American ports where it can profitably schedule its sales, it will do so on a temporary basis," Goodale told Reuters through his spokesman Vern Greenshields.
Thirty-eight ocean vessels waited to load grains at Canada's Pacific ports on Wednesday. One ship was berthed up to 41 days, CWB said.
The state grain monopoly said it faces C$15 million in demurrage fines because of the delays since early January and passed on new sales for February and March shipment.
Canadian National Railway and CP Rail System will add more locomotives to move the more than 28,300 hopper cars in their combined fleets, Goodale said.
Pacific terminal elevators will operate seven days a week begining March 1, Goodale said.
Pacific terminal elevators currently operate five days a week, Goodale said through Greenshields.
"He (Goodale) also said they're looking at the possibility of a trucking programs to Prince Rupert," Greenshields added.

Alberta Wheat Pool conducted a trial run of grain trucks to the port in Prince Rupert, British Columbia, from Alberta's Peace River Valley last summer but found the pilot project to be uneconomic at that time.
"It's not likely to be cleared up overnight. They have a clear understanding they need to make progress in the next six to eight weeks," Goodale said through Greenshields.
"The problem's been accumulating because of weather and a shortage of locomotive power and it won't be cleared up likety-split," Goodale added through Greenshields.
